title: The Kervaire conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Kervaire conjecture: adding one generator and one relation to a nontrivial group never gives the trivial group. The proof shows that for every group A and every word w in A*<t> whose exponent sum in t is +-1, the coefficient map from A to the quotient by w is injective. The first lesson states the theorem, deduces the conjecture and surveys what was known. The second builds the faithful trace on matrices over the group von Neumann algebra of an arbitrary group and proves that the trace of the spectral phase of unitaries is subadditive. The third proves, by a degree computation modulo two on an incidence manifold, that a unitary can be corrected by a block-diagonal matrix built from one unitary X and its inverse so that it fixes a subspace of the expected dimension. The fourth sets up planar surfaces made of word disks and bands, their boundary words and the Euler characteristic count; the fifth proves the planar boundary theorem by computing the phase of a boundary operator in two ways; the sixth turns a relation into such surfaces and removes them from the inside out.
prerequisites: programme lesson The spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators (course foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras), Theorems 3.1 and 8.1, Remark 4.5: the Borel functional calculus of normal operators
programme lesson C*-algebras, the continuous functional calculus, automatic continuity and positive cones (course foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras), Theorem 5.1
programme lesson Regular values and degree modulo two (course borsuks-conjecture-in-dimension-nine), Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2, Corollary 4.3: degree modulo two
core course Real Analysis II (Lebl, Basic Analysis II): Theorem 8.5.1, the inverse function theorem

programme lessons Spherical arrangements and planar intervals, Section 3, and Cone pictures and asphericity, Section 2 (course torsion-free-group-algebra-with-zero-divisors): the named statement (SURF) and the statement (PI1)

programme course Cell complexes, fundamental groups and covering spaces (cell-complexes-and-covering-spaces): lesson Fundamental groups of graphs and two-complexes, Corollary 2.4 and Theorem 3.3, which prove the statement (PI1)

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course, each with its exact statement and free locators in the lesson where it is stated: (REL) relations as maps of punctured disks: a relation g = prod b_j w^(e_j) b_j^-1 in pi_1 of a space gives a map of a disk with holes whose outer boundary reads g and whose hole boundaries read w^(e_j) (last lesson; Chen arXiv:2302.09811, Example 2.5; Hatcher Section 1.1 and Proposition 1.26); and (SURF) surfaces in the sphere, stated and not proved in the lesson Spherical arrangements and planar intervals of the course on the torsion-free group algebra with zero divisors. A foundation course proving them is requested from the programme coordinator. The statement (PI1) on fundamental groups of 2-complexes, stated in Cone pictures and asphericity of that course, is proved in the programme course cell-complexes-and-covering-spaces (Corollary 2.4 and Theorem 3.3 of the lesson Fundamental groups of graphs and two-complexes; 16 Oct 2026).
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
